newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to harmonize rules for foreign banks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to harmonize rules for foreign banks.

text.p: A decision by Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) to alter restrictions on foreign banks principally seeks to grant equal treatment to institutions operating in Brazil, a Central Bank director said.

Foreign banks are currently allowed to operate in Brazil under two distinct categories -- affilliates, which act as agencies of foreign-based banks; and subsidiaries, which are considered separate companies from their overseas parents.

Existing legislation entitles subsidiary banks to operate in more areas of the banking sector than affiliates, but the changes approved by the CMN would grant both categories equal treatment, Central Bank Norms Director Alkimar Moura said.
Another effect would be to bring Brazil's banking laws into line with those of its partners in the Mercosur customs union -- Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, Moura said.
The CMN's decision has to be ratified by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Moura said about 10 small foreign banks currently have affiliate units operating in Brazil.
